title: Cuban expedition to the Congo led by Che Guevara
summary: In April 1965, Ernesto 'Che' Guevara led an undercover force of roughly one hundred Afro-Cuban volunteers into eastern Congo across Lake Tanganyika to support anti-imperialist Simba rebels. Hampered by cultural divisions, poor communication, uncommitted local commanders, and counter-attacks by government troops accompanied by white mercenaries, the mission failed to ignite a broader revolution. Guevara withdrew his surviving troops in November 1965, recording the venture as an unmitigated failure that reshaped Cuban policy in Africa.

uncertainty.note: Guevara crossed Lake Tanganyika into the Congo on 24 April 1965 and evacuated with surviving forces on 21 November 1965.

importance.justification: Cuba's initial covert attempt to export revolutionary guerrilla warfare to the African continent, leading directly to Guevara's subsequent deployment to Bolivia.
